decision.summary: The Federal Reserve voted to maintain the target range for the federal funds rate at 0 to 1/4 percent.

changes.quote: The virus and the measures taken to protect public health have induced sharp declines in economic activity and a surge in job losses.
changes.explanation: This phrasing updates the timeline of economic damage, acknowledging that massive job losses and slowdowns have already occurred.

changes.quote: Financial conditions have improved, in part reflecting policy measures to support the economy and the flow of credit to U.S. households and businesses.
changes.explanation: The Fed noted that financial markets have stabilized somewhat thanks to previous central bank interventions and credit support.

changes.quote: To support the flow of credit to households and businesses, over coming months the Federal Reserve will increase its holdings of Treasury securities and agency residential and commercial mortgage-backed securities at least at the current pace to sustain smooth market functioning, thereby fostering effective transmission of monetary policy to broader financial conditions.
changes.explanation: The Fed clarified its ongoing commitment to buying government debt and mortgage-backed securities to keep credit flowing.

changes.quote: The Committee will closely monitor developments and is prepared to adjust its plans as appropriate.
changes.explanation: The language was broadened from monitoring market conditions to monitoring general developments as the health crisis evolves.

tone_quotes.quote: The coronavirus outbreak is causing tremendous human and economic hardship across the United States and around the world.
The ongoing public health crisis will weigh heavily on economic activity, employment, and inflation in the near term, and poses considerable risks to the economic outlook over the medium term.

for_you.text: Card rates should not move on this decision; a $5,000 balance at about 15.09% APR costs about $62.88 a month in interest.

Mortgages track the 10-year Treasury, not the fed funds rate. The 10-year was 0.75% and moved -9 bp on the day; if that move passed through, the payment on a new $300,000 30-year loan at 3.15% would fall by about $14.67 a month.
Savings yields should stay roughly where they are, since the Fed held rates.
Unemployment was 13.2%, and employers added an average of -6,418k jobs a month over the prior 3 months.

for_country.text: CPI inflation was 0.2% over the past year (May 2020); core PCE inflation, the Fed's preferred gauge, was 1%, against a 2% goal.
Real GDP grew at a -5.2% annualized pace in the latest reported quarter.
The 2-year Treasury yield, the most Fed-sensitive market rate, moved -3 bp on the day, and the S&P 500 moved -0.53%.
The broad trade-weighted dollar moved -0.06% on the day.

whats_next: The statement signals that the Fed intends to keep borrowing costs near zero until it is confident the economy has recovered from the public health crisis.

citations.detail: In light of these developments, the Committee decided to maintain the target range for the federal funds rate at 0 to 1/4 percent.

validation_notes: Forecast probabilities removed from whats_next (the page shows the live computed forecast).
